newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Samsung denies agreeing on Fokker takeover terms.
newsitem.headline: Samsung denies agreeing on Fokker takeover terms.

text.p: South Korea's Samsung Aerospace Industries on Monday denied reaching an agreement with the Dutch government over terms for a takeover of bankrupt Fokker NV, a Samsung Aerospace spokesman said.
"We are still negotiating over takeover terms but no agreement has been reached," he told Reuters.
A Samsung Aerospace executive said his company was reviewing takeover terms offered by the Amsterdam government but differences remained.
"We have put forward our takeover terms and the Dutch side has come up with terms but we are still trying to find common ground," he told Reuters.

Asked about Dutch television news on Sunday that Samsung negotiators had reached broad agreement on a takeover of Fokker, the spokesman: "It is not true. There has been nothing concrete agreed on a takeover." A Dutch government spokesman said he was not aware of any agreement on takeover terms with Samsung.

Dutch NOS television news said the Samsung negotiators, the Dutch government and administrators appointed to run the bankrupt company had set out broad terms for a takeover of Fokker in a memorandum of understanding drawn up on Friday.
In Amsterdam, Ministry of Economic Affairs spokesman Luuc van Zijp said there was no memorandum of understanding currently in preparation.

The Samsung spokesman denied the TV report that Samsung's senior management was expected to decide by Tuesday whether to approve these terms and if they did, a final agreement was expected by this coming Friday.
Fokker was declared bankrupt on March 15 after majority shareholder Daimler Benz Aerospace cut off financial aid, saying it was no longer able to bear Fokker's huge losses.

Since then Samsung Aerospace has emerged as the only serious candidate to revive Fokker's core plane-making operations. In September the administrators gave Samsung the exclusive right to examine Fokker's books with a view to a possible takeover bid.
